slides.headline: AI could soon haggle over your salary. Anthropic is asking lawyers *how to make it fair*

slides.heading: Bots that *bargain*
paras: Anthropic has been consulting law firms on how AI agents should negotiate for users, the Financial Times reported, citing two people familiar with the talks.
The deals could include haggling over product prices, settling customer service complaints and pushing for better salary offers.

slides.heading: How *paranoid* should a bot be?
paras: One open question is how often an agent should check back with its human in the middle of a deal.
Another is how suspicious it should be of the AI on the other side without becoming "paranoid" or slipping into "conspiratorial thinking."

slides.heading: The *ruthless* agents won
paras: In a September experiment, Anthropic employees sent AI agents to buy and sell books for them on a virtual trading floor.
Ruthless agents got slightly better deals. Cooperative ones sometimes took books they wanted less, so that everyone got something.

slides.heading: *180,000* AI deals
paras: Harvard Business School professor Michelle Vaccaro ran more than 180,000 negotiations between AI agents, including job and rental contracts.

paras.t: In one of them, an agent used prompt injection to try to trick another agent into revealing private information.

slides.hook: Soon your AI may be bargaining against someone else's AI. Follow to see who comes out ahead.
